title: Etale generic field model with ordinary and geometric component lower bounds
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a finite type morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Suppose $S$ is irreducible [def-weil-irreducible-components] with generic point $\eta$ [def-sc-generic-point], and put $k=\kappa(\eta)$ [def-weil-residue-field]. Fibres are scheme-theoretic [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Fix a field extension $L/k$ [def-pc-field-extension] whose spectrum map $a:\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] is finite (its coordinate algebra is a finite module) and etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Suppose $G=X_\eta\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}L$ [def-pc-fibre-product] has exactly $n$ ordinary irreducible components, for an integer $n\geq0$. There exist an irreducible scheme $T$, an etale morphism $g:T\to S$, its generic point $\xi$ with $g(\xi)=\eta$, an isomorphism $r:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\xi)\simeq\operatorname{Spec}L$, and an open subset $U\subseteq T$ containing $\xi$, such that $r$ followed by $a$ and the canonical residue-field point of $S$ equals the canonical residue-field point of $T$ followed by $g$. For $P=X\times_S T$, the projection $q:P\to T$ is finite type and this compatibility identifies $P_\xi$ with $G$. For every $t\in U$, the ordinary fibre $P_t$ has at least $n$ irreducible components; for every field extension $K/\kappa(t)$ the scheme $P_t\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)}\operatorname{Spec}K$ also has at least $n$ irreducible components. The case $n=0$ is allowed. No geometric irreducibility of the components of $G$, flatness, or Noetherian hypothesis is required.

source.place: Tag 055A (lemma-nr-geom-irreducible-components-good), proof: paragraph 2 (etale generic residue-field model) and final paragraph (ordinary lower bound and comparison with field-extended fibres); retained parent Steps 4--6.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sbc-etale-generic-residue-field-model] to the irreducible base $S$ and the supplied finite etale map $a$. Obtain $T,g,\xi,r$ and exactly the required equality of residue-field point morphisms. Here $\xi$ is generic in the whole space $T$, so $\overline{\{\xi\}}=T$. The closure of a singleton is irreducible: if it lies in a union of two closed sets, one contains $\xi$ and hence its closure. Thus $T$ is irreducible and nonempty [def-sc-generic-point, def-weil-irreducible-components].

source.place: Tag 0551 (lemma-make-components-generic-fibre-geometrically-irreducible), prescribed-field model in the proof

proof.text: Put $P=X\times_S T$. By [def-pc-scheme-fibre, def-pc-fibre-product], $P_\xi=(X\times_S T)\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\xi)$ represents pairs consisting of a map to $X$ and a map to $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\xi)$ whose composites to $S$ agree. Composing the latter with $r$ identifies these with pairs defining $G=X_\eta\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}L$, by the equality in Step 1. The inverse uses $r^{-1}$; both composites are identities by uniqueness in the pullback universal property. Hence $P_\xi\simeq G$.

source.place: Tag 055A (lemma-nr-geom-irreducible-components-good), paragraph 2, base-change identification written out

proof.text: Apply clause (2) of [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change] to $f$ and $g$. It says precisely that the projection $q:X\times_S T\to T$ is finite type, with no hypothesis on $g$.

The isomorphism in Step 2 gives $P_\xi$ exactly $n$ components. Apply [lem-trf-generic-fibre-component-lower-bound] to $q$, using Step 1 for irreducibility of $T$ and Step 3 for finite type. Obtain a nonempty open $U\subseteq T$ on which every $P_t$ has at least $n$ components. This open contains $\xi$: otherwise its closed complement contains $\xi$ and therefore $\overline{\{\xi\}}=T$, contradicting nonemptiness of $U$.

source.place: Tag 0554 (lemma-irreducible-components-in-neighbourhood), as used in the final paragraph of Tag 055A

proof.text: For $t\in U$ and any $K/\kappa(t)$, apply [lem-sfb-field-extension-irreducible-components] to the $\kappa(t)$-scheme $P_t$. It supplies a surjection from the components of $P_t\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)}\operatorname{Spec}K$ onto those of $P_t$. Choose preimages of $n$ distinct components downstairs; their images are distinct, so these preimages are distinct. This proves the required lower bound for every $K$. For $n=0$ the same assertion is vacuous, and Step 4 still applies; alternatively take $U=T$ after Steps 1--3.
